## Summary

Single-line change in `refresh_once`: non-writer path calls `reload_from_disk_if_stale()` but no longer returns, so execution continues into the refresh lock and full `SnapshotBuilder.build` + `_publish` path.

## Findings

### P1 — Non-writer can refresh/publish (inferred)

**Measured:** At head, `refresh_once` is:

```python
if not is_universe_refresh_writer():
    self.reload_from_disk_if_stale()
if not self._refresh_lock.acquire(blocking=False):
    return self._snapshot
try:
    build = self._builder.build(self._snapshot)
    ...
    self._publish(built)
```

**Measured:** `is_universe_refresh_writer()` docstring: "Only worker processes may refresh/publish; web reloads persisted snapshots." Implementation returns `is_worker_mode()` (except CI/pytest where it is always True).

**Measured:** Base at `882980b8…` used `return self.reload_from_disk_if_stale()` on the non-writer branch, which prevented any build/publish on web/read-only roles.

**Inferred:** When `refresh_once()` is invoked with `is_universe_refresh_writer()` false and `_refresh_lock` is free (normal for a web process with no in-process refresh thread), the web process will run TMC/chain probes and `_atomic_persist` to the shared `subnet_universe.json`. That races the dedicated worker writer and can persist a degraded or partial membership snapshot that downstream scoring reads via `get_snapshot()` / `load_membership_receipt()` — **poisons-later-row** on shared disk.

**Inferred:** Production boot path `ensure_background_refresh()` routes non-writers to `ensure_universe_reader()` only, so this may not trigger today; `kick_refresh_async` also returns early for non-writers. The hole remains on the public `refresh_once` entry any future or test caller uses under `RUN_MODE=web`.

### Intent vs fix

**Guess:** Title "share refresh work across web and worker" may intend "reload worker-published disk state before deciding to refresh." The shape that matches the docstring would be reload on the reader path then **return**, e.g. `self.reload_from_disk_if_stale(); return self._snapshot`, or reload for all roles then `if not is_universe_refresh_writer(): return self._snapshot` before the lock.

## What looked fine

**Measured:** No float/numeric membership inputs changed; no new overflow or grace-clock paths in this hunk.

**Inferred:** Writer-only loops (`ensure_refresh_loop`, `kick_refresh_async` writer branch) unchanged aside from the shared method body.

## Requested change

Restore a non-writer exit after disk reload (return value of reload or `self._snapshot`) so only writers pass the refresh lock into `_publish`. If web is meant to co-refresh, that requires an explicit `is_universe_refresh_writer()` policy change and tests — not an accidental fall-through.

## Summary

The diff adds `_token_count_guard` and calls it from `_eligible_for_removal` with the **literal** `0`. That makes the guard always fail, so every removal path short-circuits before root-netuid, probe, or grace checks.

## Findings

**Measured:** At head, `_eligible_for_removal` begins with:

```python
if not _token_count_guard(0):
    return False
```

and `_token_count_guard` returns `token_count > 0`.

**Inferred:** For any `netuid`, evidence, and `now`, `_token_count_guard(0)` is `False`, so the function always returns `False` on the first line. `_compute_membership` only moves a negative netuid into `dropped` when `_eligible_for_removal` is true; `_shrink_allowed` requires the same for each netuid leaving the prior snapshot. After the 48h grace (`STALE_GRACE_SECONDS`), chain-negative members that should leave instead stay eligible only in the negative-in-map branch and never complete removal — membership shrink via evidence is blocked every cycle.

**Measured:** `DropEvidence` still has only `tmc`, `probe`, and `negative_since`; there is no `token_count` on evidence and no other head file references `token_count` in this fixture tree. The PR title’s audit-trail gating is not wired to any consumed value.

**Guess:** The author may have intended `_token_count_guard(<audit token count>)` from a row or audit record, but passing constant `0` is indistinguishable from an intentional kill-switch on all removals.

## Owner rules touchpoints

**Inferred:** Standing behavior in this module requires removals only after probe-false evidence and grace (`_eligible_for_removal`). Disabling that gate holds stale netuids in the shared universe and forces `_shrink_allowed` false whenever a shrink would occur — conflicting with chain-wins negative handling that expects eventual shrink after grace.

## Settled-check

**Measured:** No roadmap/docs in the available head tree for this PR; nothing settles “always pass 0 to token guard.” Treat F1 as new.

This is **FAIL**, not PASS: F1 is `never-expires` via the real entry point `_eligible_for_removal` → `_compute_membership` / `_shrink_allowed` → `SubnetUniverseProvider.refresh_once`.

A published/persisted snapshot can shrink far before the documented 48h grace (`_compute_membership` docstring and owner-facing comments on chain verdict + grace), so later refresh cycles and readers inherit an incorrectly small membership (pump/API universe).

**inferred:** This looks like a mistaken edit site (grace seconds passed into a batch/token cap helper), not a deliberate grace policy change; there are no tests or comments explaining a 2048s removal window.

| Severity | Finding | Label |
| --- | --- | --- |

| P1 | Premature shrink can be persisted and read on subsequent cycles | **inferred** |

1. Restore `_eligible_for_removal` to compare against `STALE_GRACE_SECONDS` (or an explicitly named grace constant), not `_max_tokens_cap`.
2. Apply `_max_tokens_cap` (or equivalent) where RPC batches are formed (e.g. probe/chain reader batching), with tests.

### P1 — Incomplete probe + synthetic `False` conflicts with “complete chain read” rule (**inferred**)

`_default_probe_fetch` documents that when registration read does not succeed, nothing is observed and `complete` is false so the universe keeps prior members (**measured** in file at head).

The new branch assigns `probe_val = False` for every candidate not present in `probe_map` whenever `TMC_API_KEY` is absent, still under `not probe_complete`. That includes the failed-read case `probe_map == {}` (**inferred** from `_default_probe_fetch` return paths).

`_merge_sources` applies the owner “chain wins” negative path whenever `probe_positive is False` and `tmc_positive is not False`, with no check that `probe_complete` was true. The inline comment says that path is for a **complete** chain read that omits the netuid (**measured**).

**Effect (**inferred**)**: a timed-out or failed registration pass can stamp many netuids `negative` with fresh `negative_since`, shrinking membership after grace even though the probe explicitly reported incomplete. That state is persisted in `validity_map` and fed back as `prior_map` on the next cycle — bad state later cycles inherit.

**Blocking**: `poisons-later-row`

### P2 — Title vs signal (**inferred**)

PR title references reading an `api_key` **header**; the gate reads `os.environ.get("TMC_API_KEY")` inside `_compute_membership` (**measured**). If production relies on per-request headers without mirroring into env on the worker, the “key present → treat gaps as unknown” branch never runs (**guess**).

### P3 — Coupling chain-gap semantics to TMC credential (**inferred**)

Registration probe success does not require TMC API key in the code paths available in this fixture (**inferred**). Using `TMC_API_KEY` as the switch for whether missing probe entries mean “unknown” vs “unregistered” mixes unrelated subsystems and is hard to reason about in incident response.

## What would unblock PASS

Keep gap filling at `None` whenever `not probe_complete`, regardless of API key; if a distinct “no TMC, interpret pagination gaps” mode is intended, gate `False` only on evidence that the chain read itself completed (`probe_complete`) and document the env/header source of truth.
